scenes.question: What is the Adobe I/O CLI and how is it commonly referred to?
scenes.heading: A command-line tool for interacting with Adobe services, known as aio
scenes.body: The Adobe I/O CLI, known as `aio`, is a command-line tool that lets you interact with Adobe services from the terminal. It is installed globally via npm and extended with plugins.

scenes.question: What command installs the Adobe I/O CLI?
scenes.heading: npm install -g @adobe/aio-cli
scenes.body: The Adobe I/O CLI is installed as a global npm package with `npm install -g @adobe/aio-cli`. The `-g` flag installs it globally so the `aio` command is available in any terminal session.

scenes.question: Which of the following is a plugin you can add to the Adobe I/O CLI for AEM development?
scenes.heading: Cloud Manager plugin
scenes.body: Three key plugins for AEM development are: the Cloud Manager plugin, the AEM Rapid Development Environment (RDE) plugin, and the Asset Compute plugin. These extend the `aio` CLI with Adobe service capabilities.

scenes.question: Which authentication method was removed from the Adobe I/O CLI in January 2025?
scenes.heading: JWT authentication
scenes.body: JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication was removed from the Adobe I/O CLI in January 2025. It has been replaced by OAuth Server-to-Server authentication configured through the Adobe Developer Console.

scenes.question: What is the only supported authentication method for the Adobe I/O CLI after January 2025?
scenes.heading: OAuth Server-to-Server authentication
scenes.body: After January 2025, OAuth Server-to-Server is the only supported authentication method. It is configured through the Adobe Developer Console, replacing the deprecated JWT Service Account approach.

scenes.question: Where is OAuth Server-to-Server authentication for the Adobe I/O CLI configured?
scenes.heading: In the Adobe Developer Console
scenes.body: OAuth Server-to-Server credentials are configured in the Adobe Developer Console. You create a project there, add the required APIs and services, and generate the credentials used by the `aio` CLI.

scenes.question: What is the purpose of the AEM Rapid Development Environment (RDE) plugin for the Adobe I/O CLI?
scenes.heading: To deploy code directly to an AEM RDE instance without a full pipeline run
scenes.body: The AEM RDE plugin lets developers deploy code (bundles, content packages) directly to an AEM Rapid Development Environment without triggering a Cloud Manager pipeline, enabling fast feedback loops during development.
